propositions: Test plants a young index.lock and uses threading.Timer to unlink it, but the timer fires while git holds its own real index.lock during commit, causing the delete to remove git's lock mid-operation
On slow runners (macOS py3.13 leg ~23m vs Linux ~12m), git commit is still holding index.lock when the 0.4s timer fires, resulting in 'fatal: unable to write new index file'
The timer body has no identity check to distinguish the planted lock from git's real lock, so it unconditionally unlinks whatever exists at t=0.4
Test should use gitutil._retry_probe instead of threading.Timer to release the planted lock deterministically after the first retry attempt, eliminating wall-clock timing dependence
This is a test-local race, not a product defect: production code behaves correctly with force_reclaim=True, and runner resource exhaustion is ruled out
